en: Thus have I heard— The Shorter Discourse on the Cowherd (Cūḷagopālakasutta), Majjhima Nikāya 34.
On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling among the Vajjis at Ukkacelā on the bank of the river Gaṅgā.
There the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus: “Bhikkhus!”
“Venerable Sir,” those bhikkhus replied to the Blessed One.
The Blessed One said this:
“Once upon a time, bhikkhus, there was a cowherd from Magadha who was dull-witted. In the last month of the rainy season...”
In the autumn season, without looking back at the near bank of the river Gaṅgā and without looking toward the far bank,
he drove the cattle across at a place that was not a ford, toward the opposite shore in the land of Videha. Then, monks, the cattle,
having formed a circle in the middle of the current of the river Gaṅgā, met with ruin and disaster right there.
And why is that? Because, monks, that cowherd of Magadha was of poor wisdom;
in the last month of the rains, during the autumn season, he had not examined the near bank of the river Ganges, nor had he examined the far bank.
Just as one might urge cattle across to the far shore by means of a place that is not a ford,
even so, monks, whatever ascetics or brahmins are unskilled in this world,
unskilled in the other world, unskilled in the realm of Māra, unskilled in the realm beyond Māra, and unskilled in the realm of Death— [they are like those who seek to cross by a non-ford].
They are unwholesome for the domain of ministers; for those who think they should listen to them and place their trust in them, that will lead to their harm and suffering for a long time.
Once in the past, monks, there was a wise Magadhan cowherd during the last month of the rainy season.
In the autumn season, having surveyed the near bank of the river Gaṅgā and having surveyed the far bank,
he drove the cattle across to the further shore of the Videhas at a very suitable ford.
First, he drove across those bulls who were the fathers of the herd and the leaders of the herd.
Having cut across the current of the Ganges, they reached the further shore in safety.
Then he drove on other powerful bulls and tamable bulls;
they too, having cut across the current of the Ganges, reached the further shore in safety.
Then he caused other calves, even younger calves, to cross.
They too, having cut across the current of the Ganges, reached the further shore in safety.
Then he caused other calves, those that were weaklings, to cross.
Having cut across the current of the Ganges from one bank, they reached the further shore in safety.

Once in the past, monks, there was a young calf, just born, who, while being carried away by the current of his mother cow, also cut across the current of the Ganges from one bank and reached the further shore in safety.
For what reason was that?
For that cowherd of Magadha, monks, was naturally wise; in the last month of the rains,
during the autumn season, having surveyed the near bank of the river Ganges and having surveyed the far bank,
he drove the cattle across at a very shallow ford to the opposite shore of the Videhas.
In the same way, monks, whatever recluses or brahmins are skilled regarding this world and skilled regarding the other world,
skilled regarding the realm of Māra and skilled regarding that which is not the realm of Māra,
skilled regarding the realm of Death and skilled regarding that which is not the realm of Death— those who think they should listen to them and place faith in them, for them that will come to pass.
for their welfare and happiness for a long time.
Just as those bulls, monks, who are fathers of the herd and leaders of the herd, having cut across the current of the Ganges, reached the further shore in safety;
even so, monks, those bhikkhus who are arahants, whose taints are exhausted, who have lived the holy life, and who have done what was to be done—

Having laid down the burden, accomplished their own goal, completely destroyed the fetters of existence, and liberated through right knowledge, they have cut across the stream of Māra horizontally and reached the further shore in safety.
Just as those powerful, well-trained oxen, monks, having cut across the stream of the Ganges horizontally, went safely to the further shore; so too have they.
In the same way, monks, those bhikkhus who, through the complete destruction of the five lower fetters,
are of spontaneous birth, attaining final nibbāna there, not subject to returning from that world— they too, having cut through Māra’s ear-hole across,
will go safely to the further shore.
"Just as those young bulls and young cows, bhikkhus, having cut across the current of the Ganges,
reached the further shore in safety; even so, bhikkhus, those bhikkhus who, through the total destruction of three fetters and the attenuation of lust, hate, and delusion,
are once-returners and will return to this world only once more to make an end of suffering— they too, having cut across [the stream]..."
Having cut across Māra’s stream, they will go safely to the further shore.
Just as those young calves, bhikkhus, who were lean and weak, cut across the stream of the Ganges and went safely to the further shore,

even so, bhikkhus, those bhikkhus who, through the total destruction of the three fetters, are stream-enterers, no longer subject to rebirth in the lower worlds, fixed in destiny, with enlightenment as their destination— they too, having cut across Māra’s stream, will go safely to the further shore.
“Just as that young calf, monks, having been born only a short while ago, being carried along by his mother’s tail, cut across the current of the Ganges and reached the further shore in safety;
even so, monks, those bhikkhus who are followers of the Dhamma and followers by faith will also cut across Māra’s stream and reach the further shore in safety.
And I, monks, am skilled in this world and skilled in the other world, skilled in the realm of Māra.”
“I am skilled in the realm of Māra, skilled in the realm of Death, and skilled in the realm beyond Death.
For those who think my words should be heard and believed, monks, that will lead to their welfare and happiness for a long time.
Thus spoke the Blessed One.
Having said this, the Sugata, the Teacher, further spoke these words:
“This world and the world beyond have been well-expounded by the Knower.”
Having directly known the entire world— that which has been reached by Māra and that which has not yet been reached by Death—
By the Fully Awakened One, the Knower,
the door to the Deathless has been opened for the attainment of the secure Nibbāna.
The stream of the Evil One is cut off,
shattered and rendered useless;
be full of gladness.
“O bhikkhus, you have attained security.
The Cūḷagopālakasutta, the fourth, is finished.
